builder.title: The poll's name. It appears on your dashboard, in your poll list and as a small heading for participants.
builder.description: Optional intro for the whole poll. Participants read it before the first question; your dashboard and the display show it under the heading. Up to 1000 characters.
builder.question: The question participants answer. They always see it exactly as you write it.
builder.label: A short name for this question wherever you present results: dashboard, display, group comparison, moderation and the column names in exports. Participants never see it. If you leave it empty, the question text is used instead.
builder.help: Optional extra line below the question, for example an example answer or a format. Only participants see it.
builder.required: On: participants must answer before they can continue. Off: they can skip this question.
builder.optional: Extras you can skip: a short field label for your presentation and a hint for participants.
builder.more: Settings that depend on the question type, such as step limits.

type.trace: Participants list the steps of a process in order, for example their morning. The process model, variants and consensus are built from these answers.
type.single_choice: Participants pick exactly one option, for example a role. You can compare the processes of the groups it creates.
type.multiple_choice: Participants pick one or more options. You can compare processes by it, but people who pick several options count in each of those groups.
type.number: Participants enter a number, for example an age. Add group boundaries to compare processes between ranges.
type.text: Participants write free text. It is only exported, not analysed. Ask for opinions, not for personal data.

builder.traceMode: Free entry: people type their steps in their own words. Select & sort: people arrange steps from a list you provide, which gives cleaner data but less variety.
builder.traceSteps: The fewest and the most steps one answer may have (1 to 50).
builder.traceMaxLabel: Longest allowed name for a single step, in characters (10 to 120).
builder.traceRepeats: Lets someone use the same step more than once, for example a second coffee. Repeats show up as loops in the process model.
builder.traceSkip: People don't have to use every step you offer; they can leave some out.
builder.traceSuggest: While typing, people see steps that others already entered. That reduces different spellings but can nudge everyone towards the same wording (anchoring). Turn it off if you study how people phrase things on their own.
builder.traceCustom: People may add their own steps in addition to your list.
builder.tracePool: The steps people choose from, one per line (at least 2).
builder.options: The choices participants see, one per line (2 to 30). Every choice must be different.
builder.maxSelected: Limits how many options one person may tick. Leave empty for no limit.
builder.numberRange: Smallest and largest number people may enter. Leave empty for no limit.
builder.numberInteger: On: only whole numbers. Off: decimals are allowed.
builder.numberBins: Boundaries that cut the numbers into ranges. 18, 25, 40 gives four ranges: below 18, from 18 up to 25, from 25 up to 40 and 40 or more. Needed to compare processes by this number.
builder.textMax: Longest answer in characters. Free text can contain personal data, so participants are asked not to enter any.

settings.resultsPublic: On: after answering, participants can open the live results. Off: only you and the display link show them.
settings.allowResubmit: On: people can change their answer later and the new answer replaces the old one. Off: one answer per person.
settings.retention: Up to 365 days in normal operation. In the public demo, polls are kept for 7 days from creation, even if still running.
settings.kMin: The smallest group that may be shown in a comparison. Groups with fewer responses are hidden so that single people can't be recognised from their answers. Higher means more privacy but more hidden groups.

kpi.responses: People who submitted an answer. This can be fewer than the number who joined, because some only open the poll.
kpi.variants: How many different sequences were given. Two answers are the same variant only if the steps and their order are identical.
kpi.topVariant: Share of all responses that gave the most common sequence. A high value means people agree on how the process runs.

tabs.variants: Every distinct sequence of steps with how many people gave it, most common first.
tabs.flow: The process model: boxes are steps, arrows show how often one step directly follows another.
tabs.consensus: Where most people agree on what comes next, where they split, and the most typical complete process.
tabs.groups: Compare the processes of groups of people, for example by role or experience.

dfg.topVariants: Highlights complete paths from the most frequent variants, from start to end. Other parts of the model remain visible with less contrast.
dfg.paths: Highlights the most frequent arrows. Other paths remain visible with less contrast.
dfg.metric: How arrows are labelled. Absolute shows the number of transitions. Percent shows each transition's share among all arrows leaving the same step.
dfg.fullscreen: Shows the process model across the whole screen. Press Esc to leave.

consensus.strong: Steps where clearly most people continue the same way: reliably above 70 %, including a safety margin for small samples.
consensus.divergence: Steps after which people take different routes, sorted by how many answers deviate from the most common continuation.
consensus.medoid: The real answer that is on average closest to all others. The number tells how far the answers differ from it: 0 is identical, 1 is completely different.
consensus.lowSupport: Steps that appear too rarely to say anything reliable about what follows them.

compare.groupBy: The question that splits people into groups. Only choice questions and numbers with group boundaries can be used.
compare.view: Side by side shows the process of each group. Difference shows only transitions that are more common in one group, coloured by that group.
compare.hiddenGroups: Groups smaller than the minimum group size are hidden so single people stay anonymous. You can change the size in Settings.
compare.minDelta: Hides transitions whose share differs by less than this many percentage points between the groups.
compare.stats: Δ is the gap between the highest and the lowest share. p tells how likely such a gap is by chance, q corrects that for the many transitions tested. Treat both as hints, not as proof.
compare.pairwise: How different two groups are overall, from 0 (same) to 1 (completely different). With few answers even identical groups show some difference.

moderation.merge: Merging treats different spellings as one step, for example "e-mail" and "Email". Raw answers stay unchanged; only the analysis and the exports change.
moderation.hide: Hidden labels are left out of the analysis and the exports, for example nonsense entries. You can show them again.
moderation.suggestions: Proposed from similar spelling. Nothing changes until you accept and save.

export.csv: One row per step for spreadsheets, R or Python. Contains the typed text, the merged label and one column per other question, named by its field label.
export.xes: Standard event log for process mining tools. The timestamps are synthetic: they follow the order of the steps, not real times, so do not interpret durations.
export.json: Complete data dump with poll, questions, answers and merges, for archiving or your own analysis.

host.joined: Joined: people who opened the poll. Responses: people who actually submitted. Usually fewer, because some leave early.
host.hostLink: The host link opens the dashboard with full control: results, export, settings and delete. Keep it private. For a projector use the read-only display link from the menu under "Display mode".
host.displayLink: A read-only view for a projector or screen sharing. It shows results but can't change or export anything, and it does not contain your host key. The host link gives full control, so never share that one.
host.traceSelect: Switch which process question the results below are about.
host.editTexts: Fix typos or sharpen the wording at any time, even while the poll is live. Question type and answer options stay locked once the poll has started.
